title: Counting low eigenvalues of tangential Dirichlet Witten Laplacians on compact oriented manifolds with Morse potentials and locally characteristic critical boundary points
source_title: Eyring-Kramers exit rates for the overdamped Langevin dynamics: the case with saddle points on the boundary
author: Tony Lelièvre; Dorian Le Peutrec; Boris Nectoux
difficulty_reason: The standard interior and noncharacteristic Witten models do not cover actual Morse critical points on the boundary where the normal derivative vanishes. The authors construct a new characteristic half-space model without simultaneously block-diagonalizing the potential and metric, and establish the degree-dependent normal-mode kernel and uniform spectral gap through the complete localized splitting and metric-comparison argument. Their new model determines exactly which negative normal Hessian points contribute an index shift, then the fully written localization and spectral projection estimates exclude any extra small eigenforms.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Theorem4 under Assumption(M-f): smooth compact connected oriented Riemannian manifold with boundary; smooth f and its boundary restriction are Morse, and the normal derivative of f vanishes on a boundary neighborhood of every boundary critical point of f. For every degree q, the spectrum in [0,c h] has dimension m_q for sufficiently small h, where m_q counts interior index-q points, boundary restriction index-(q-1) points with positive normal derivative, and actual critical boundary points with boundary index(q-1) and negative normal Hessian eigenvalue, exactly49. Full new half-space model proof22–37 and manifold localization/finite-dimensional comparison proof37–42 read. The new characteristic-boundary core is retained; earlier noncharacteristic/interior models are explicitly traced to references42 Chapter3 and44, with whole-space Proposition18 references42 Propositions3.3.2/3.3.3 and41 Proposition2.2. Lemma22 metric freezing35 explicitly follows published reference42 Lemma3.3.7; its displayed smooth metric/norm comparison and standard quadratic-form estimate are traced background rather than an independently reconstructed new core. Named IMS, min-max and spectral projection lemma11 supply routine functional analysis. No full exit-rate/Eyring–Kramers asymptotics, quasi-mode boundary flux construction in unreviewed Section3, or non-reversible diffusion assertion counted. Whole103-page original context retained; original2025volume12 DOI10.5802/jep.303 and acquisition dates checked and unchanged.

historical_source_pdf_evidence.original_difficulty_reason: The authors analyze half-space Witten complexes at actual boundary critical points using localized tensor comparison, spectral supersymmetry and metric freezing, then glue local models through IMS localization and min-max estimates. This semiclassical boundary spectral analysis exceeds ordinary qualifying examinations.
